title: Handoff Is a Conversation
intro: Bring engineers in early and agree what done means. The spec covers every state.

learn.title: Not a baton pass
learn.text:
A finished file thrown over the wall arrives with decisions nobody can question.

**Shift left:** engineers join critiques and early sketches.

options: Designs move to a left-aligned grid
Handoff moves to the end of the sprint

learn.title: Definition of done
learn.text:
Agree **before** handoff which states, breakpoints, accessibility checks and content are included.

Use the **lightest process** that works.

try.q: When should the definition of done be agreed?
options: At the end of the quarter

learn.title: Every state
learn.text:
Empty, loading, partial, error, success, disabled, read-only.
Longest name, zero items and a thousand, missing images, 30% longer translations.

try.q: Which is most often missing from specs?
options: The primary button and its hover style
try.explain: Edge states are where handoff bugs hide.

learn.title: The test
learn.text:
If an engineer could build it **without asking a question**, the spec is complete.

If they would have to guess, the guess is your design.

try.q: An engineer has to guess a loading state. Whose design is it?
options: The design system’s default, applied automatically
try.explain: Unspecified states get designed by whoever builds them.

test.q: Handoff fails most when treated as:
test.explain: Questions arrive in the last week.

options: The lightest steps that work for your team
A heavy, standard template applied to every project
The process of the largest team

test.q: A design departs from the system. What to do?
options: Say where and why in the spec
test.explain: Work from the system, explain departures.

test.q: Which content edge case belongs in a spec?
Which accessibility items belong in a spec?
options: Animation easing curves and their durations only

test.q: What single change do teams most report helps?
options: More detailed redlines on every screen
